correctness.rationale: An independent exact replay used the seven explicit lines, all 2^7 and 3^7 maps with labeled colors, and the no-monochromatic-line condition, which allows three distinct colors on a line. It found 0 and 882 proper colorings, respectively. Legal single-coordinate changes and a separate all-pairs Hamming-one test produced identical edges; there are 3906, with counts 252, 504, 126 at degrees 8, 9, 10. All 882 BFS traversals of this graph visited all states, with maximum distance 7 for every source. The 388521 unordered pairs had excess d-h exactly 0 in 386253 cases and 1 in 2268 cases; symmetry gives the ordered-pair bound, and diagonal pairs have zero excess. The claimed h=5,d=6 and h=d=7 witnesses were recovered; every step of the printed six-move path independently satisfies the line constraints. Explicit permutation testing of the seven lines found the full 168-element point group, and its action together with all six palette permutations gave one orbit per listed profile, with sizes 126,252,504 for (1,2,4),(1,3,3),(2,2,3). Replay code for the full finite calculation is supplied at review_evidence/3/replay_fano_independent.py (run with Python 3 from the workspace); the uploaded script was inspected, not executed. Independently, for inclusion–exclusion any nonempty chosen line set has one connected block on its union. Three lines are concurrent in 7 of 35 cases (union size 7 instead of 6); four lines omit one point in exactly 7 of 35 cases and never omit two; five or more cover all points. With singles and pairs covering 3 and 5 points this gives q^7-7q^5+21q^3-21q^2+6q. All claims are for this fixed seven-point object.

value.rationale: The canonical seven-point non-two-colorable triple system at the first feasible palette size is a natural test case for coloring reconfiguration. Knowing connectivity alone does not answer whether direct Hamming-optimal recoloring is always possible. The precise negative answer, sharp one-extra-move bound, and full exception count give a reusable benchmark for proposed geodesic or shortest-path claims. The finite classification is motivated by those metric facts rather than simply recomputing a color count or claiming a broader hypergraph theorem.
